questions.q: Where do you start creating a Trailhead account?
options: trailhead.salesforce.com, by clicking Sign Up in the top right
Only inside the Salesforce mobile app
By calling Salesforce support and requesting an account
Through the AppExchange checkout page
questions.explain: Sign-up starts at trailhead.salesforce.com, using the Sign Up button in the top right of the real, live site.

questions.q: Why does this lesson warn against signing up for Trailhead with a Salesforce trial org login?
options: Trial orgs expire and can't be reactivated, so you'd lose access to the Trailhead account tied to it
Trial orgs are more expensive than Developer Edition orgs
Trial org logins are not accepted by Trailhead at all
Trial orgs require a credit card to sign up for Trailhead
questions.explain: Trial orgs expire on a fixed schedule and can't be reactivated, which would cost you access to the Trailhead account tied to that login.

questions.q: Is a credit card required anywhere in the Trailhead sign-up flow, per this lesson?
options: No — a Trailhead account on its own doesn't include a Salesforce org yet, so there's no credit card step
Yes, a valid credit card is required to finish sign-up
Only if you sign up using a business email
Only if you plan to use Developer Edition later
questions.explain: The sign-up flow never asks for a credit card, since the Trailhead account alone doesn't grant a Salesforce org.

questions.q: What does this lesson say about the default Profile Privacy setting on a new Trailhead account?
options: It defaults to Public, which is normal and is what lets your badges function as a portfolio
It defaults to Private and cannot be changed
It defaults to Public and cannot be changed
There is no privacy setting available on Trailhead accounts
questions.explain: New accounts default to Public profile visibility, which the lesson notes is normal and useful for showing badges to employers later, though it can be switched to Private any time.

questions.q: Why does this lesson say your Trailhead username choice matters?
options: It becomes part of your public Trailblazer profile URL, which can later function as a real portfolio
It determines which Salesforce edition you're allowed to use
It is only visible to Salesforce employees
It cannot be changed under any circumstances, even by contacting support
questions.explain: The username becomes part of the public Trailblazer profile URL, which is why the lesson suggests picking something you wouldn't mind an employer seeing.
